title: Outlook desktop: Create PDF from email that keeps the sensitivity label
summary: Hold for a missing licensing qualification: Microsoft says users assigned premium or Plan 2 information-protection licences must also have the corresponding Standard or Plan 1 licence assigned. The roadmap facts, control paths and registry settings are supported; the page correctly leaves the new export's encryption handling and default unresolved.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Outlook Desktop blocks printing labelled email to PDF when mandatory labelling is enabled.
claims.quote: Outlook Desktop blocks printing to PDF if Mandatory Labeling is enabled. ... This error occurs when a label is applied to the email.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The support article dates the mandatory-labelling Print to PDF block to January 2024.
claims.quote: This change is in all M365 channels beginning in January 2024.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The August 2024 support article says Outlook Desktop does not support exporting files to PDF.
claims.quote: This error can be misleading since Outlook Desktop does not support exporting files to PDF.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: The support article says Outlook Desktop cannot print PDF files with the sensitivity label applied.
claims.quote: Outlook Desktop does not have the capability to print PDF files with the label applied. The label is not preserved when the email is printed to PDF.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The existing Print to PDF route removes the sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Because this option removes the sensitivity label, this option won't be available to users if you're using mandatory labeling.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The existing Print to PDF route loses encryption if the label applies it.
claims.quote: If users select this option, they are warned that the document or email will lose the protection of the label, and encryption (if applied), and must confirm to continue.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Word, Excel and PowerPoint for Windows support exporting Office documents to PDF.
claims.quote: Office for Windows: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint support the following methods to convert an Office document into a PDF document: ... File > Export > PDF

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Those exported PDFs inherit the source label and its content markings.
claims.quote: When the PDF is created, it inherits the label with any content markings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn says Outlook does not currently support PDF attachments inheriting encryption from a labelled message.
claims.quote: Outlook doesn't currently support PDF attachments inheriting encryption from a labeled message.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Encrypted PDFs created by the documented Office export can be opened with Microsoft Edge on Windows or Mac.
claims.quote: For Windows, if the label applied encryption, that encryption is also inherited. Encrypted PDFs can be opened with Microsoft Edge on Windows or Mac.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: rendered mandatory labelling row
claims.claim: The full Purview route through Publishing policies, policy, Edit Policy and Policy settings reaches Require users to apply a label to their email or documents.
claims.quote: In the label policy configuration from the Microsoft Purview portal, on the Policy settings page: Select Require users to apply a label to their email or documents.

claims.where: controls[0].ui: route into an existing label policy
claims.claim: The first part of that route is Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > policy > Edit Policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. ... To edit an existing label policy, select it, and then select the Edit Policy button from the flyout pane:

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: rendered mandatory labelling row
claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity <policy> -AdvancedSettings @{DisableMandatoryInOutlook="True"} exempts Outlook messages from mandatory labelling in supported Outlook apps.
claims.quote: DisableMandatoryInOutlook: Outlook apps that support this setting exempt Outlook messages from mandatory labeling. Example: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{DisableMandatoryInOutlook="True"}.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Mandatory labelling is set per sensitivity label policy and applies to users assigned that policy.
claims.quote: When the policy setting Require users to apply a label to their email and documents is selected, users assigned the policy must select and apply a sensitivity label in their Office apps:

claims.where: controls[0].note
claims.claim: Learn describes clearing a checkbox to exempt emails from mandatory labelling in Outlook apps that support the option.
claims.quote: Then select Next > Next and clear the checkbox Require users to apply a label to their emails. Keep the checkbox selected if you want mandatory labeling to apply to emails as well as to documents.

claims.where: controls[0].note
claims.claim: DisableMandatoryInOutlook exempts Outlook messages rather than configuring mandatory labelling for documents.
claims.quote: DisableMandatoryInOutlook: Outlook apps that support this setting exempt Outlook messages from mandatory labeling.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].note; Governance controls: rendered Office policy row
claims.claim: Group Policy contains the quoted Office 2016 Save As PDF and XPS add-ins path and Sensitivity feature setting, which is configured as Disabled.
claims.quote: Group Policy Office setting under User Configuration/Administrative Templates/Microsoft Office 2016/Microsoft Save As PDF and Save As XPS add-ins: ... Use the Sensitivity feature in Office to apply sensitivity labels to PDFs ... Configure this setting to be Disabled.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Setting HKCU\software\policies\microsoft\office\16.0\common\fixedformat disablepdfprotection to DWORD 1 disables label and encryption handling for Office PDF creation.
claims.quote: Group Policy registry path: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\software\policies\microsoft\office\16.0\common\fixedformat DWORD: disablepdfprotection Value: 1

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls: rendered Outlook registry row
claims.claim: No admin UI setting is documented for the Outlook-only label-discarding Print to PDF registry workaround.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook "disablepdfprotectioninoutlook" "Group Policy"; "Print to PDF is blocked if Mandatory Labeling is enabled" "disablepdfprotectioninoutlook". Opened the support article and Office sensitivity-label documentation; they give the Outlook registry key, not an admin UI setting.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Outlook\Preferences disablepdfprotectioninoutlook DWORD 1 enables printing to PDF without preserving the label or encryption.
claims.quote: Path: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Outlook\Preferences Name: disablepdfprotectioninoutlook (dword32) Value: 1

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls: rendered Outlook registry row
claims.claim: The disablepdfprotectioninoutlook workaround applies only to Outlook Desktop.
claims.quote: The Outlook Team implemented a new registry key that only applies to Outlook Desktop. It enables printing to PDF without preserving the label or encryption.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Office disablepdfprotection policy disables saving with sensitivity labels and encryption for both Print to PDF and export.
claims.quote: Disable the Office policy setting that applies sensitivity labels and encryption to PDF files. The registry key disables saving with labels for both the Print to PDF as well as the export option in the Office applications.

claims.quote: If you need to disable the PDF support in Office apps for Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, you can do so by using a Group Policy Office setting

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: manual-labelling plan list
claims.claim: Manual Sensitivity Labeling is Included in the listed Microsoft 365, OneDrive, EMS, Office 365 and AIP Plan 1 and Plan 2 plans.

claims.fix: Keep the accurate Included table and plan list, but append this qualification to the licensing notes and the paragraph listing plans: 'For Information Protection for Office 365 and AIP, a Standard/Plan 1 licence must also be assigned alongside a premium/Plan 2 licence for users to access sensitivity labelling.'
